story.title: Drums Across the Field
story.text: The Qi army drummed across the field, and Duke Zhuang wanted to charge.
story.narration: On the field of Changshao the Qi army began to beat their drums. Duke Zhuang clenched his fists and wanted to charge at once — Cao Gui held his hand down.

story.title: Wait a Little Longer
story.text: Cao Gui held his hand: wait — wait until their third drumming is over.
story.narration: One drum, two drums, three drums. Cao Gui said: wait a little longer. A battle turns on courage — the first drumming stirs it, the second wears it thin, the third leaves them spent. When their strength is gone, we move.

keyMoment.question: The first drum sounds. Charge?

options.hint: They are fired up — you would meet them at their strongest.

options.text: No — wait until their third drumming is done

options.hint: Their drums would be wasted — but you would miss the moment to move as well.

keyMoment.reveal: Wait until the other side is tired, then move — the easiest way to win.

misconceptions: Rushing in first is what brave looks like

quiz.question: After which drumming did Cao Gui let the army move?
quiz.explanation: The first drumming stirs courage, the second wears it thin, the third leaves them spent — so they waited for the third.

quiz.question: According to the Zuo Zhuan, what does a battle depend on?
quiz.explanation: In battle, courage is what counts — and courage runs out.

quiz.question: In a tug of war, when is it easiest to pull?
options: Give it everything at the start
Wait until the other side has spent most of their strength
quiz.explanation: Let them spend their strength first, then pull — that is waiting at ease.
